venue.name: The Whale Centre
venue.description: The Whale Centre runs guided wildlife boat tours from an office at 411 Campbell Street in downtown Tofino. Whale watching runs March to November and bear watching runs April to October, both two and a half hours, on either a heated cabin cruiser or an open Boston Whaler. Tours are booked online, by phone or in person at the office, and every passenger including infants needs a ticket. The site describes no museum, display or walk-in visit at the address, and publishes no school or daycare rate.
venue.address: 411 Campbell Street, Tofino, British Columbia V0R 2Z0

facility_notes.washrooms: Yes, restroom facilities are available at the dock and at the hot springs pools, as well as change rooms.
facility_notes.rain_backup: Tours run in the rain and are only cancelled in extreme or unsafe conditions. The cabin cruiser has a heated indoor cabin and seating, with protection from wind and rain.

restrictions: Infants and small children are not able to go out on the open boat.
All passengers, including infants, require a ticket. Age and size restrictions may apply for safety reasons.
Participants must be 19 years of age or require a parent or guardian to sign on their behalf.
Tours require a minimum number of guests to operate.
venue.hours_notes: The office at 411 Campbell Street is open Monday to Sunday, 8:00 am to 6:00 pm. Check in at least 30 minutes before your tour departure time.
venue.seasonal_notes: Whale watching tours run March to November. Bear watching tours run April to October.

programs.name: Whale watching boat tour
programs.description: A two and a half hour guided boat tour in Clayoquot Sound looking for grey whales, humpback whales, killer whales, sea otters, seals and bald eagles, with a full narrative from the guide. It runs March to November, with multiple departures a day shown on the booking calendar. You choose between the heated cabin cruiser, which has an indoor cabin and seating, and the open Boston Whaler, which supplies full Mustang floater suits. Prices are per person and do not include taxes, fees or gratuities.
programs.what_children_do: Check in at the Campbell Street office, sign waivers and get fitted, then either sit in the heated cabin or stand in a floater suit on the open boat. They stay on the boat for two and a half hours while a guide talks about the whales, the wildlife and the history, watching for grey whales, humpbacks, killer whales, sea otters, seals and bald eagles.
programs.our_note: It is two and a half hours on a boat with no way off, and check in is half an hour before that, so it takes most of a morning. The open boat is not an option for infants and small children, so a young group needs the heated cabin cruiser. Ask about the youngest age they will take before you plan anything, because the site only says age and size restrictions may apply.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are at the dock and the cabin cruiser is heated and enclosed, and the per person prices are published with the extra fees spelled out. Nothing about a minimum age, a group or school rate, lunch space or wheelchair access is stated anywhere, so a call is worth it.
programs.extra_fees_note: Prices displayed do not include taxes, fees or gratuities for the guides. The booking policy lists 5% GST, a $3.00 Clayoquot Sound Access Fee per person, a $10.00 fuel surcharge per person, and 6% FareHarbor website fees.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hours notice is required for a full refund. Late cancellations are charged the full amount to the card on file.

programs.name: Bear watching boat tour
programs.description: A two and a half hour guided boat tour along the shoreline of Clayoquot Sound looking for black bears, running April to October. Departures follow the low tide and change from day to day, so the times are on the booking calendar rather than published as a schedule. The tour runs on calm, protected waters, on a heated cabin cruiser, an open Boston Whaler or a larger cruiser. Prices are per person and do not include taxes, fees or gratuities.
programs.what_children_do: Ride a boat for two and a half hours close to the shore at low tide, watching the rocks and the forest edge for black bears while a guide talks. On the cabin cruiser they sit inside a heated cabin; on the open boat they wear a full floater suit. Bald eagles and seals are also on the way.
programs.our_note: The boat goes out on the low tide, so the departure time moves through the week and you will not know yours until you look at their calendar. That makes it hard to fit around nap times and pickup. Infants and small children cannot go on the open boat, so ask for the heated cabin cruiser when you call.
programs.practical_summary: The price, the season, the two and a half hour length and the twelve person boat limit are all published, and the water is described as calm and protected. There is no stated minimum age, no group or school rate, and nothing about lunch, strollers or wheelchairs, so those need a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Prices displayed do not include taxes, fees or gratuities for the guides. The booking policy lists 5% GST, a $3.00 Clayoquot Sound Access Fee per person, a $10.00 fuel surcharge per person, and 6% FareHarbor website fees.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hours notice is required for a full refund. Late cancellations are charged the full amount to the card on file.
programs.evidence: Infants and small children are not able to go out on the open boat

programs.name: Private charter for a group
programs.description: The whale watching and bear watching tour pages both list a private tour for up to 12 guests at $1,800, which holds the boat for one group instead of selling seats. The price is per boat and does not include taxes, fees or gratuities. Private bookings need 72 hours notice to cancel for a full refund, rather than the 48 hours on a scheduled tour. The site does not say which tours can be chartered, what months it runs, or whether a school or daycare can book one.
programs.what_children_do: The same two and a half hour boat trip as a scheduled departure, with the boat held for one group of up to twelve rather than shared with other passengers.
programs.our_note: This buys the whole boat for up to twelve people, which lands close to the cost of twelve children's tickets on a scheduled departure. Worth asking which works out better once you count the adults you have to bring. Nothing on the site says whether they take daycare or school bookings at all, so start there.
programs.practical_summary: The charter price and the twelve person limit are published, and cancellation needs three days notice instead of two. Which tours can be chartered, what months, and whether children's groups are welcome are all unstated, so this one needs a phone call before anything else.
programs.extra_fees_note: Prices displayed do not include taxes, fees or gratuities for the guides. The booking policy lists 5% GST, a $3.00 Clayoquot Sound Access Fee per person, a $10.00 fuel surcharge per person, and 6% FareHarbor website fees.
programs.cancellation_note: 72 hours notice is required for a full refund on a private tour. Late cancellations are charged the full amount to the card on file.
